The outlined treatment plan for Grace's osteoarthritis is highly appropriate and aligns with standard clinical guidelines. Osteoarthritis management typically focuses on symptom relief and improving joint function without invasive procedures. Taking over-the-counter pain relievers (such as acetaminophen or NSAIDs) is a first-line approach for managing pain. Low-impact aerobic exercises like swimming and biking are recommended because they improve cardiovascular health and joint mobility while minimizing stress on the knee joints. Furthermore, physical therapy focused on strengthening the muscles around the knees helps stabilize the joint, reduces load on the cartilage, and can significantly decrease pain and improve function. This conservative, multimodal approach is considered best practice for initial management of knee osteoarthritis.
